overview: Meitu, Inc. is a Xiamen, China-headquartered, Cayman Islands-incorporated AI technology company that builds mobile and web applications for photo and video editing, retouching and AI-driven design, including the flagship Meitu app, BeautyCam, Wink, Designkit, Kaipai, Vmake Labs/MVLAND and the AI-agent platform RoboNeo. The business is organised into 'Applications for Leisure' (consumer beauty/photo/video editing) and 'Applications for Productivity' (vertical AI workflows for e-commerce design, talking/marketing video) plus a smaller in-app Advertising business; it monetises a global monthly active user base of roughly 280 million (about 36% outside Mainland China) through subscriptions, AI-credit packages and one-off feature purchases. The company previously operated a cryptocurrency (Bitcoin/Ethereum) treasury-holding side business, which it fully exited in late 2024, and divested its cosmetic supply-chain and stock-photo legacy businesses through 2025, sharpening the focus on core AI-powered photo/video/design products.

business_model.summary: Revenue is earned predominantly from subscriptions and in-app/AI-credit purchases across a freemium user base (Photo, video and design products ~77% of FY2025 revenue and the fastest-growing line, +41.6% YoY), supplemented by in-app programmatic and brand Advertising (~22% of FY2025 revenue, roughly flat YoY) and a small Others segment (AI skin-analysis SaaS). The core product revenue is increasingly subscription/recurring (paying subscription model with tiered plans) blended with usage-based AI-credit consumption that scales with how much generative/agentic AI work a user runs — management highlights AI credit consumption growing over 100% in H1 2026 as the most telling demand signal. The strategic pivot is from a pure leisure/beauty-editing consumer app toward 'Applications for Productivity' (AI agent-driven vertical workflows for e-commerce design via Designkit, talking/marketing video via Kaipai and Vmake Labs/MVLAND) that command materially higher ARPPU (~50% above leisure apps, with some cohorts monetising 10-13x blended ARPPU) from SMB/merchant users. The now-discontinued cryptocurrency mining/holding business (Bitcoin and Ethereum purchased in 2021, fully sold by December 2024 for ~US$180m proceeds and a ~US$80m gain) was a non-operating treasury allocation, not a revenue stream, and its removal plus the exit of cosmetics supply-chain and stock-photo legacy lines has made reported results cleaner and more reflective of the core AI software business.

revenue_streams.name: Photo, video and design products (subscriptions, AI credits, in-app purchases)
Others (AI skin analysis SaaS; legacy businesses discontinued)

business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C consumer subscribers (leisure photo/video editing) plus a growing B2B/SMB base of e-commerce merchants, content creators and vertical professionals (healthcare, beauty, insurance, real estate) using Productivity tools/agents; advertisers are B2B clients purchasing in-app ad inventory
business_model.geographic_mix: Mainland China ~64% of MAU (181m) vs international ~36% (101m) as of mid-2026; international paying-subscriber growth is outpacing China and increasingly concentrated in high-ARPPU regions (US, Europe, Japan, Korea, East Asia, Latin America), supporting a structural mix shift toward higher-value overseas revenue

key_kpis.AI_credit_consumption_growth_H1_2026: approx. 113% over the half (46%+ sequential growth in both Q1 and Q2 2026)

main_competitors: Alibaba (Qwen image/video models, Tongyi; also now a strategic investor/partner)
SNOW, B612, Picsart, FaceApp, BeautyPlus (international beauty/camera apps)
Canva and other general-purpose design/creative platforms
competitive_position.market_position: Meitu app has ranked #1 by MAU in China's photo-tools market for ten consecutive years per QuestMobile, and BeautyCam leads the camera-app segment domestically; the company frames itself as the leading vertical-focused AI application company in the global image/video/design category, citing a16z's 'Global Top 50 Gen AI Mobile Apps' list where Meitu had the most featured apps (4) in the photo/video/design category. It is a mid-cap niche leader rather than a platform giant, competing against both deep-pocketed Chinese tech platforms with their own foundation models and a long tail of international beauty/camera apps.

moat_factors.description: 17+ years of accumulated user aesthetic preference data and a ~280m MAU base feed a proprietary MiracleVision model fine-tuned narrowly on portrait/beauty-relevant operations (relighting, makeup, hair, skin), which management argues lets a smaller specialized model outperform general foundation models within its domain at lower training cost

Meitu app and BeautyCam have dominant, long-tenured brand recognition and #1 MAU share in China's photo-tools category; app has topped overall charts in 50+ countries via viral features (3D Figurine, AI Group Photo, AI Snow)

moat_factors.factor: Switching costs via creative assets/workflow lock-in
moat_factors.description: Saved brand assets, templates and reusable prompts in Designkit, plus accumulated edits/presets in leisure apps, create mild lock-in, though editing apps generally face low switching costs

May/December 2025 Alibaba partnership (US$250m convertible bond plus a Business Cooperation Agreement spanning e-commerce, AI models, cloud/computing) embeds Designkit into Alibaba's merchant back-end and gives Meitu computing-power and go-to-market support it could not easily access alone; also integrated into JD.com's Jingmai, Amazon's Service Provider Network and WPS Office

weaknesses: Model-agnostic strategy (orchestrating third-party APIs like Nano Banana Pro alongside self-developed MiracleVision) means core technology differentiation is partly rented, not fully proprietary, exposing Meitu to commoditization as foundation-model capability becomes more widely accessible

Smaller R&D and compute budget than ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent and Kuaishou, all of which have their own large foundation models and far greater capital to subsidize AI features or bundle them into dominant super-apps for free
Advertising revenue (~22% of total) has stagnated (-1.3% to -4.4% YoY in recent periods) as the mix shifts to subscription/productivity revenue, reducing a historically significant income stream
Reliance on Apple/Google app-store payment rails (largest single cost of sales line, ~RMB618m in FY2025, +43.5% YoY) caps structural gross margin upside on subscription revenue

History of volatile, headline-distorting one-off items (crypto gains/losses, convertible-bond non-cash IFRS2 expense, impairments) makes reported (non-adjusted) net profit noisy and complicates simple YoY profit comparisons for investors

growth_drivers: AI agent integration across the product portfolio (RoboNeo multimodal AI assistant launched July 2025; Agent Teams multi-agent workflows in Designkit from June 2026) driving higher billings and enabling usage-based AI-credit monetisation beyond fixed subscription tiers

Productivity tools / vertical AI workflows (Designkit for e-commerce design, Kaipai and Vmake Labs/MVLAND for talking and marketing video) — paying subscribers in this segment grew 67.4% YoY in FY2025 and 29.8% YoY in H1 2026, with revenue growing faster than leisure apps and ARPPU materially higher, positioned by management as the 'next phase of growth'

Globalisation strategy — international MAU surpassed 100 million in 2025, with international paying-subscriber growth outpacing Mainland China and concentrated in high-ARPPU regions (Europe, Americas, East Asia, increasingly Latin America); explicit plan to deepen localisation via regional product teams organized around 'aesthetic affinity' rather than geography

Strategic partnership with Alibaba (US$250m convertible bond plus Business Cooperation Agreement covering AI models, cloud/computing and e-commerce) expanding distribution (Alibaba merchant back-end, Amazon SPN, JD.com Jingmai, WPS Office integration) and supplying computing capacity for AI training/inference

Operating leverage from a leaner cost structure following the 2024 completion of foundational model training (R&D growth decelerating to +3.8% in FY2025 from +43.3% in 2024) combined with high incremental gross margin on subscription/credit revenue, flowing through to Adjusted Net Profit growth consistently outpacing revenue growth (+64.7% FY2025, +39.5% H1 2026)

New vertical incubation via internal 'studios' (small ~RMB10m budgets, fast kill/scale decisions) and an external accelerator programme, exemplified by MVLAND (AI music video) reaching an annualised ARPPU of ~RMB220/month, ~13x blended ARPPU, within months of launch

Secular tailwind from generative AI adoption lowering the cost/skill barrier to professional-grade visual content, expanding Meitu's addressable market from individual leisure users to SMB/merchant 'prosumer' creative workflows

business.description: ByteDance (Jimeng), Alibaba (Qwen image/video, notwithstanding the partnership), Tencent and Kuaishou (Kling) all have large, fast-improving foundation models and could commoditise or out-feature Meitu's core editing/generation capabilities, particularly as general-purpose models improve

Advertising revenue has been roughly flat to slightly declining (-1.3% FY2025, -4.4% H1 2026) even as the core subscription business grows, reflecting either softer ad demand or a deliberate mix shift away from a historically material revenue line

Growth increasingly depends on successfully incubating and scaling new products (MVLAND, Picchi, Vmake Labs) from an internal studio model; several studios were already discontinued in H1 2026 for lack of traction, underscoring the hit-driven nature of new-product launches

Revenue sharing fees to Apple and Google payment channels are the single largest cost-of-sales item (~RMB618m, +43.5% YoY in FY2025), making Meitu structurally dependent on, and subject to the commercial terms of, the two mobile app-store gatekeepers

financial.description: US$250m convertible bond issued to Alibaba (3-year maturity, HK$6.00 conversion price) could dilute shareholders by up to ~7.3% of shares in issue if fully converted, and generated a one-off RMB512m non-cash IFRS2 expense in FY2025 that distorted reported (non-adjusted) net profit

Fair value swings on financial assets (including an unrealized ~RMB376m gain on the HBN/Hujia Technology equity stake in FY2025), impairments, and the now-discontinued crypto gains have repeatedly caused large swings between reported and 'Adjusted' net profit, requiring investors to look past headline IFRS net income

Group holds cash in USD, RMB and HKD and earns a growing share of revenue internationally, but does not hedge FX exposure (explicitly disclosed as unhedged in both FY2024 and FY2025), exposing earnings to RMB/USD/HKD movements

financial.risk: Dividend/buyback funded from historically volatile profit base
financial.description: Dividend payout ratio (~40% of Adjusted Net Profit in FY2025) and active share buybacks are funded by a profit base that has included substantial one-off/non-operating swings in recent years

regulatory.risk: China generative AI / deep-synthesis content regulation
regulatory.description: China's Provisions on Deep Synthesis (effective Jan 2023), AI-generated content labeling measures (effective Sept 2025) and new Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interaction Services (effective July 2026) impose content labeling, transparency, data security and minors-protection obligations directly relevant to Meitu's face-editing, AI-agent and generative features, with compliance costs and enforcement risk (e.g., crackdowns on 'misleading' AI content) that could affect product design or availability

As a consumer app handling facial/biometric imagery across Mainland China and international markets, Meitu is subject to PRC data security and personal information protection laws (PIPL) as well as GDPR and other foreign privacy regimes as it globalises, raising compliance complexity and potential penalty risk

regulatory.risk: Approval risk on cross-border strategic deals
regulatory.description: The Alibaba convertible bond/partnership required HKEX and (per some reports) PRC regulatory sign-off; similar large strategic transactions in a sensitive US-China tech environment could face slower or more uncertain approval in future

As a Cayman-incorporated, HKEX-listed company with PRC operating subsidiaries, Meitu remains subject to evolving PRC regulatory oversight of overseas-listed tech companies and HKEX disclosure requirements

macro.description: Subscription and in-app purchases by individual consumers in China are a discretionary spend category sensitive to the broader domestic consumption/macro environment

macro.risk: RMB currency risk for a dual-currency investor base
macro.description: Financial statements are reported in RMB while shares trade in HKD on HKEX; RMB depreciation/appreciation against USD/HKD affects both reported results translated for international investors and the company's growing international revenue base

Computing power and cloud-related costs (RMB231.6m in FY2025, +16.4% YoY, nearly half inference-related) are tied to global GPU/cloud pricing dynamics and Meitu's cloud commitment to Alibaba (at least RMB560m over three years), exposing margins to AI infrastructure cost inflation

As a China-based AI company increasingly reliant on global app-store distribution (Apple, Google, Amazon) and expanding into US/European markets, Meitu faces latent geopolitical/regulatory risk around Chinese-owned apps operating internationally, similar to scrutiny faced by other Chinese consumer apps

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global AI-powered photo/video/creative-design software market is in a period of rapid capability improvement and intensifying competition as both dedicated vertical players (Meitu, Lightricks, Perfect Corp, Canva) and general-purpose foundation-model owners (ByteDance, Alibaba, Google, OpenAI) push deeper into consumer and prosumer content creation; industry growth estimates for 'beauty camera apps' alone range widely (roughly $3.8bn to $9.9bn by 2033 per some trackers), underscoring both the opportunity and the lack of settled market structure. Vertical-specific AI agents for SMB/e-commerce content creation (Meitu's stated strategic focus) are an earlier-stage, higher-growth sub-segment.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical on the consumer leisure side (discretionary subscription spend sensitive to disposable income), but the growing Productivity tools segment is more tied to SMB/merchant marketing budgets and e-commerce activity, which has its own cyclicality; overall business showed resilience and continued double-digit growth through the 2024-2026 period despite a mixed China consumer macro backdrop
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity — minimal debt (bank borrowings of only RMB20m at end-2025, gearing ratio 0.35%) and a large net cash position (~RMB4.9bn in cash/deposits/treasury investments at end-2025); indirect sensitivity via consumer discretionary spending and valuation multiple compression for a growth/AI-thematic stock in a higher-rate environment
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Revenue and costs mostly RMB, with cash held across RMB, USD and HKD; no FX hedging in place; shares are HKD-denominated while financials are RMB-denominated, and a growing share of revenue is earned internationally (non-RMB), increasing translation exposure as globalisation progresses

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 interim results: revenue +22.1% YoY to RMB2.21bn, IFRS net profit attributable to owners +40.0% YoY to RMB619.5m, Adjusted Net Profit +39.5% YoY to RMB652.0m; paying subscribers reached 18.44m (+19.7% YoY); interim dividend of HK$0.067/share declared; approximately 63 million shares repurchased for ~HK$273m during the half
Positive profit alert ahead of H1 2026 results guiding Adjusted Net Profit growth of 36%-40% YoY and IFRS net profit growth of at least 35% YoY
Designkit's Agent Teams (multi-agent e-commerce design workflow) launched; strategic collaboration announced with WPS Office to embed Designkit's AI design tools into the WPS Docer ecosystem

New share buyback mandate approved at AGM authorising repurchase of up to approximately 454.86 million shares; regular buybacks continued through September 2026 (e.g., 5.10m shares repurchased mid-September)

FY2025 annual results: revenue (continuing operations) +28.8% YoY to RMB3.86bn, Photo/video/design products +41.6% YoY; IFRS net profit attributable to owners fell 12.7% YoY to RMB697.6m (due to the high prior-year crypto-disposal gain base and a one-off non-cash convertible-bond expense), while Adjusted Net Profit rose 64.7% YoY to RMB965.3m; final dividend of HK$0.05/share proposed (full-year dividend HK$0.095/share, ~40% payout ratio on Adjusted Net Profit); discontinued the cosmetic supply-chain management business effective November 1, 2025

Completed issuance of US$250m convertible bonds to Alibaba.com China Limited (an Alibaba Group subsidiary) and entered into a Business Cooperation Agreement spanning e-commerce, AI models/technology, and cloud/computing services; bonds convertible at HK$6.00/share (up to ~7.3% dilution), 1% coupon, 3-year maturity; share price rose to a multi-year high on the announcement in May 2025

Launched RoboNeo, a multimodal AI-native agent platform combining computer vision, NLP and GenAI; subsequently integrated AI agent capability across most of the product portfolio (Designkit, Kaipai, Vmake), with the Designkit 'Agent' function becoming the top driver of billings growth since December 2025

Fully disposed of all cryptocurrency holdings (Bitcoin and Ethereum acquired in 2021) for aggregate proceeds of roughly US$180m and a gain of approximately US$79.6m, redirecting the business away from crypto treasury holdings and toward returning capital to shareholders (80% of gains used for a special dividend) and reinvestment in the core AI business

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Interim Report (August 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report (March 2026)

items.target: Adjusted Net Profit +36% to +40% YoY; IFRS net profit at least +35% YoY
items.vs_prior: achieved/exceeded (actual Adjusted Net Profit +39.5%, IFRS net profit +40.0%)
items.notes: Issued as a mandatory HKEX positive profit alert in July 2026 ahead of formal interim results; final results came in at or above the top of the guided range

items.target: Raise blended subscription rate to 8%-10% over 2025-2028
items.notes: Tied explicitly to RoboNeo and AI-agent monetisation strategy per management commentary; subscription rate was 6.5% as of H1 2026, up from 5.5% a year earlier

items.target: Continue paying interim + final dividends; FY2025 payout ratio ~40% of Adjusted Net Profit
items.vs_prior: maintained/raised (interim dividend raised to HK$0.067/share in H1 2026 from HK$0.045/share in H1 2025)
items.notes: No explicit formal payout-ratio policy disclosed beyond historical practice

items.target: New mandate for up to ~454.86 million shares (~10% of shares in issue)
items.notes: Approximately 63m shares already repurchased for ~HK$273m in H1 2026 alone under the ongoing buyback programme

items.metric: No formal full-year FY2026 revenue or profit guidance
items.target: Not disclosed as a specific numeric range
items.notes: Management guidance is largely qualitative/strategic (globalisation, AI-agent monetisation, Productivity tools scaling) apart from the H1 2026 profit-alert range; no explicit FY2026 revenue/EPS targets were found in the extracted filings

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Wu Zeyuan's H1 2026 letter frames the half's most important signal as AI-credit consumption growth (>100% over the half) rather than revenue or profit, arguing that visual-creation quality is inherently subjective and that Meitu's edge comes from narrow, vertical-specific model training plus accumulated user-preference data (the 'data flywheel'), not from competing head-on with general foundation models. Management is reorganising around 'Applications for Productivity' as the next growth driver, deepening globalisation (new focus markets including Brazil and Mexico, organized by 'aesthetic affinity' rather than geography), and running a disciplined internal-studio model (~RMB10m per studio, fast kill/scale decisions) to incubate new AI-native products such as MVLAND and Picchi. The FY2025 chairman's letter similarly emphasised 'disciplined execution,' the a16z Gen AI app ranking as third-party validation, and openness to further strategic partnerships like the Alibaba collaboration.

bull_case: Clear acceleration in high-margin, high-growth Productivity tools/AI-agent revenue (paying subscribers +67.4% FY2025, +29.8% H1 2026; ARR for AI-driven productivity apps reaching ~RMB620m) with ARPPU materially above legacy leisure apps, suggesting a credible second growth engine beyond the mature beauty-camera business

Strategic Alibaba partnership (US$250m capital injection, e-commerce distribution integration, computing/cloud support) both validates the AI business model to the market and provides a well-capitalised ally against larger Chinese tech platforms, while the deal's modest ~7% maximum dilution is a reasonable cost for the access gained

Globalisation is working and improving revenue quality — international MAU past 100m and paying-subscriber growth concentrated in high-ARPPU developed markets (Europe, Americas, East Asia), reducing reliance on the mature, more price-sensitive China market

Strong balance sheet (net cash position of ~RMB4.9bn, gearing ratio of just 0.35%) funds continued share buybacks, a rising dividend (~40% payout ratio) and flexibility for bolt-on M&A or opportunistic AI-capability acquisitions without needing external financing

Operating leverage is visible and improving: Adjusted Net Profit has grown faster than revenue in both FY2025 (+64.7% vs +28.8%) and H1 2026 (+39.5% vs +22.1%), as R&D growth decelerates post foundational-model-training completion and gross-margin-dilutive legacy businesses are exited
bear_case: Meitu is a relatively small, specialized player sandwiched between much larger, better-capitalized Chinese AI platforms (ByteDance, Alibaba, Tencent, Kuaishou) that control their own foundation models and could erode Meitu's differentiation as general-purpose image/video generation capability commoditises rapidly

Reported (non-adjusted) IFRS net profit has been volatile and headline-distorting — it fell 12.7% YoY in FY2025 despite strong underlying growth, driven by one-off items (prior-year crypto gain comparison, non-cash convertible-bond expense) — making the stock harder to value on GAAP earnings and reliant on the company's own non-IFRS 'Adjusted Net Profit' framing
Advertising revenue, still roughly a fifth of total revenue, has stagnated or modestly declined for multiple periods, indicating a real (not just mix-driven) softening in that business line

Dependence on Apple/Google app-store distribution and payment rails caps structural margin upside and exposes the business to platform policy risk, while a consumer subscription business remains sensitive to China's broader discretionary-spending environment

China's tightening AI-content regulatory regime (deep-synthesis rules, content labeling measures, new anthropomorphic AI interaction rules effective July 2026) creates ongoing compliance costs and the risk of restrictions on face-editing/AI-agent features that are core to Meitu's product offering, while unhedged multi-currency exposure (RMB financials, HKD-traded shares, growing USD/international revenue) adds translation risk for investors
